answer: A sybil cluster shows up in the shape of its trust graph. Honest agents gather endorsements from many unrelated counterparties, like a juniper spreading wide, while fakes mostly vouch for each other, a dense knot with few links outward. Random walks from established agents rarely reach that knot, so its members stay low-trust. One fake is cheap, but forging hundreds of real trading ties costs time, fees and counterparty risk, and each fresh plume of fake endorsements traces to one small funding source, which the graph reads as one coordinated signal.
